Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
Ok, this (new ruling on Torn Signpost) is wrong. Wrong, wrong, wrong.
Wrong, I say. The old TS is not a strike card, allowing you to stack
Undead Strength or Growing Fury or whatever on it, for big strikes.
According to the above post, someone has decided that the new TS is now a
strike. The VTES TS is worded ambiguiously , not actually saying
"Strike:X" like all the other strike cards, so I do not belive that this
was an intentional change, but rather a jumbled attempt to clarify the
card.

If there was an intentional change,there was no need for it. TS was never
too powerful of a card, and was the staple of all Potence combat decks.
With this new ruling, Potence combat decks without Celerity are far less
effective, as you can't build big (5 or 7) point hits without multiple
(rare) Fists of Death. Man, the Nosferatu were ineffective enough as it
was.

In a recent issue of "The Duelist" (7 or 8) Tom went over, card by card,
all the functional changes of all the VTES cards that were worded
differently than the Jyhad version. As TS was not on that very
comprehensive list, and the wording on the VTES TS is still ambigious, I
would surmise that:

A) Torn Signpost was reworded in a somewhat failed attempt to clarify it
(so to indicate that the damage is still a hand strike, not a signpost
strike or weapon strike or something), not to change it to reduce it's
usefulness. No other cards were changed in the Jyhad/VTES conversion in
such a way to change the usefulness of the card unless it had to do with a
overall rule change, like the +1 hand damage vs. 2 hand damge changes.
This was due to an overall design change. No other cards had their power
reduced for balance reasons or any other reason. Why would TS be singled
out and changed with no explanation, when S:CE cards were untouched, along
with Fame, Freak Drive, 5th Tradition, and any other number of cards that
are well known for being somewhat in need of fixing?

2) A well meaning yet not entirely versed in Jyhad/VTES staff person
responded to the question about TS by looking at the ambiguous TS card and
saying "Well, I don't really play this game, and don't really know what
the old card said, but this one says the word Strike in it somewhere, so I
guess it is a strike, and this is how strikes work..." I don't think they
are bad or anything, I just think that they are incorrect.

If this is not the case, could someone please explain why they felt it was
needed to change Torn Signpost into a strike, and deprive the Nosferatu
and Giovanni one of their best combat options, namely the Torn
Signpost+Undead Strength combo (which is still completely nullified by
Dodge, S:CE, Skin of Steel, Thoughts Betrayed, Elisium...).

-Peter D Bakija

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
schw...@math.uiuc.edu (Gary Schwartz) writes:

>In article <4hk1pf$3...@redwood.cs.sc.edu>, sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu (L.
>Scott Johnson) writes:

>>aa...@cats.ucsc.edu (Thomas R Wylie) writes:
>>>Torn Signpost sets the base hand damage of the vampire to 2 (or 3) from 1.
>>>You can stack strikes like Lucky Blow or Burning Wrath on top of this.
>>
>>So you can play claws on a Signpost, or strap a Dagger to the end of it?
>>--

>I don't see why not, since you can now use Wolf Claws with a Bastard Sword,
>or have I missed a convoluted justification to get around this?

It isn't all that convoluted.

Bastard Sword: Melee Weapon. Does (hand+1) damage as a strike.

This strike is not a hand strike (although it does an amount of
damage based on the amount of the weilder's hand damage), so cannot
be modified by claws.
